key_insight: An ordinal AI model graded 25 lumbar MRI degeneration tasks and improved external exact accuracy by 6.3 percentage points over a softmax-based counterpart.
clinical_relevance: Automated grading could support screening and triage, but prospective clinical benefit remains unproven.
method: Analyzed 24 sagittal T2-weighted slices per examination using full-sequence multi-instance learning.
Combined ResNet34 features, a bidirectional GRU, and attention pooling.
Used 25 ordinal output heads for five conditions across five disc levels.
evidence_signal: Trained on 1,204 examinations and internally validated on 213, the model achieved 64.9% external exact accuracy versus 58.6% for its comparator in 60 independent hospital patients without fine-tuning.
watch_item: External validation was small and used radiology reports as the reference standard; broader prospective evaluation is needed.
paper_title: Ordinal Multi-Instance Learning for Automated Multi-Task Grading of Lumbar Degenerative Conditions on Sagittal MRI, with External Validation
